# Interval Cinema: quiet pause room

## Project
- Commission name: INTERVAL CINEMA
- Space: independent quiet pause room beside the screening corridor
- Users: cinema visitors and companions seeking a short break before or after a screening
- Decision: room arrangement and fit-out installation brief
- Room sign: Quiet pause
- Return cue: Cinema corridor
- Drawing and specification sheet name: INTERVAL CINEMA

## Fixed room geometry
- Units: metres
- Origin: inside southwest floor corner
- Axes: x east; y north; z upward
- Interior extents: x=0–8; y=0–6; z=0–3
- Internal dimensions: 8.0 m by 6.0 m
- Clear ceiling height: 3.0 m

| ID | Position | Dimensions and condition |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | South wall; x=1.2–2.4; z=0–2.2 | Open entrance; 1.2 m wide; 2.2 m high; connection to cinema corridor |
| W1 | North wall; x=5.2–7.2; z=1.0–2.5 | Window; 2.0 m wide; 1.5 m high; sill 1.0 m above floor |
| C1 | x=3.8–4.2; y=3.3–3.7; z=0–3 | Full-height column; 0.4 m square |

- Retained elements: boundary, ceiling, entrance opening, window opening and column
- Interior additions available: nonstructural partitions; adjustable shade at W1
- D1 operating condition: continuously open entrance
- Corridor: existing adjoining context

## Capacity and movement
| Place | Seated capacity | Belongings provision | Spatial relationship |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 1 | 1 reachable spot | Visual buffer from D1 and P1; open access |
| S2 | 1 | 1 reachable spot | Visual buffer from D1 and P1; open access |
| P1 | 2 | 1 reachable spot for 2 bags | Companion conversation |

- Total seated capacity: 4
- Total belongings spots: 3
- Continuous clear route: at least 1.2 m wide between D1, S1, S2 and P1
- Connected clear turning circle: at least 1.5 m diameter
- Clear movement area: space clear of furniture, column, screens and stored bags

## Sensory and operational conditions
- Corridor activity: active during room use
- Daylight source: W1
- Acoustic response location: near the south, corridor-facing boundary
- Window response: adjustable interior shade
- Electric lighting character: diffuse, steady, shielded or indirect at seated eye level
- Lighting layers: ambient; local reading; entrance cue
- Lighting control: independent layer control; clearly located visitor brightness control
- Surface selection: cleanable contact surfaces with stated cleaning methods
- Visual hierarchy: restrained pattern contrast
- Furniture, palette, materials and exact layout: open design choices
- Shared drawing references: material IDs and luminaire IDs

## Visitor views
| View | Eye position in m | Target in m | Occupancy | Visible landmarks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | (0.8,2.2,1.6) | (4.8,4.5,1.3) | 1 visitor at S1 | W1 wall and C1 |
| B | (7.3,5.2,1.6) | (2.4,1.4,1.2) | 4 visitors across S1, S2 and P1 | D1 and C1 |

- Source-guide horizontal field of view: 84 degrees
- Perspective A annotation: readable acoustic-material ID
- Perspective B signs: Quiet pause; Cinema corridor

# INTERVAL CINEMA — delivery catalog

This table lists every commissioned deliverable with its tier, file format and stage. What each deliverable must contain is stated in the commission letter.

| # | id | Deliverable | Tiers | Format and stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | furnished-plan | Furnished room and circulation plan | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 2 | entrance-section | Entrance and acoustic treatment sectional elevation | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 3 | lighting-plan | Reflected ceiling and lighting plan | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 4 | materials-furniture | Material and furniture specification sheet | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 5 | visitor-view-a | Individual pause perspective from camera A | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 6 | visitor-view-b | Full occupancy and return perspective from camera B | 6 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |

# Interval Cinema: existing room

## Room record
- Space: empty cinema room envelope
- Furniture, partitions, finishes and lighting: open design choices
- Source-view grid and neutral colors: spatial reading aids
- Dimensional authority: existing-plan.png and numeric room records

## Fixed geometry
- Units: metres
- Origin: inside southwest floor corner
- Axes: x east; y north; z upward
- Inside room: x=0–8; y=0–6; z=0–3
- Internal dimensions: 8.0 m by 6.0 m
- Clear ceiling: 3.0 m
- Retained geometry: boundary, ceiling, entrance, window and column
- Wall opening inventory: D1 and W1

| ID | Fixed position | Clear dimensions |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | South wall, x=1.2–2.4, z=0–2.2 | Entrance 1.2 m wide, 2.2 m high; connection to existing cinema corridor |
| W1 | North wall, x=5.2–7.2, z=1.0–2.5 | Window 2.0 m wide and 1.5 m high; sill 1.0 m above floor |
| C1 | x=3.8–4.2, y=3.3–3.7, z=0–3 | Full-height square column, 0.4 m by 0.4 m |

## Retention and additions
| Element | Existing condition | Design scope |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Open entrance | Continued open connection to corridor |
| Existing corridor | Adjoining cinema circulation | Context outside the room fit-out |
| W1 | Original window geometry | Adjustable interior shade; original window identified behind shade |
| C1 | Continuous full-height column | Original position, section and height |
| Room interior | Empty envelope | New nonstructural partitions available |

## Supplied views
| Image | Content | Guide eye in m | Guide target in m | Guide horizontal field of view |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| existing-plan.png | Dimensioned schematic plan with north and camera arrows | — | — | — |
| existing-view-a.png | Empty-room context toward north/east; W1 and C1 | (0.8,2.2,1.6) | (4.8,4.5,1.3) | 84 degrees |
| existing-view-b.png | Empty-room context toward southwest; D1 and C1 | (7.3,5.2,1.6) | (2.4,1.4,1.2) | 84 degrees |

- Perspective preparation: AI generation guided by native room views
- Coordinates: native-guide camera positions and targets
- Perspective reference role: complementary landmark relationships and neutral empty-room appearance
- Camera scope in source room record: positions within the room
- North-facing view landmarks: W1 wall and C1
- Return-view landmarks: D1 and C1
- Retained-feature notation behind new elements: light outline or callout

# Interval Cinema: people and operations

## Purpose
- Client: Interval Cinema
- Space: quiet pause room beside the screening corridor
- Users: visitors and companions seeking a short break from cinema brightness, movement and sound
- Use: general rest and companion conversation
- Supplied evidence: room geometry and operating brief

## Capacity and use
| Place | Function | Seated people | Belongings spot | Relationship |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Individual rest | 1 | 1 reachable spot | Visual buffer from D1 and P1; open connection to room |
| S2 | Individual rest | 1 | 1 reachable spot | Visual buffer from D1 and P1; open connection to room |
| P1 | Companion conversation | 2 | 1 reachable spot holding 2 bags | Shared conversation place |

- Total seated people: 4
- Total belongings spots: 3
- Buffer options: turned seat, screen, low partition or another coherent spatial arrangement
- Individual-place character: open resting places
- Furniture forms, layout and exact placement: designer-selected
- Belongings location: outside circulation space

## Circulation
| Item | Planning dimension | Connection |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous clear route | At least 1.2 m wide | D1 to S1, S2 and P1 and back to the corridor |
| Clear turning circle | At least 1.5 m diameter | Connected to the continuous clear route |

- Dimension locations: narrowest route segments and turning circle
- Occupied footprints: furniture, column, screens and stored bags
- Clear space: area outside occupied footprints

## Sensory and operating conditions
| Condition | Room response |
|---|---|
| Active corridor outside D1 during use | Acoustic treatment near the corridor-facing boundary |
| Daylight entering only through W1 | Adjustable shading treatment at W1 |
| Open entrance | Clear return route through D1 |
| Electric lighting | Diffuse illumination; steady output; light sources shielded or directed away from seated eyes |
| Visitor adjustment | Clearly located brightness control |
| Drawing information | Luminaire locations, light direction and distinguishable daylight and electric light |
| Visual hierarchy | Restrained pattern contrast; open palette and style |
| Contact surfaces | Cleanable finishes with stated cleaning approaches |

- Treatment descriptions: intended acoustic and shading functions
- Acoustic and glare information: qualitative treatment intent
- Material information: selected surface and intended maintenance method
- Cinema identity scope: room signs and project identification

## Fixed sign text
| Location | Function | Exact text |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Room identification | Quiet pause |
| D1 | Return cue | Cinema corridor |

- Return perspective content: both signs

steps.userMessage:
INTERVAL CINEMA | Quiet pause room beside the screening corridor

We are fitting out an existing room at Interval Cinema for visitors who need a short pause before or after a screening. Its internal dimensions are 8.0 m east–west by 6.0 m north–south, with a 3.0 m clear ceiling. The origin is the inside southwest floor corner; x runs east, y north and z upward. D1 is the open south-wall entrance at x=1.2–2.4, z=0–2.2, measuring 1.2 m wide by 2.2 m high. W1 is the north-wall window at x=5.2–7.2, z=1.0–2.5, measuring 2.0 m wide by 1.5 m high with a 1.0 m sill. C1 occupies x=3.8–4.2, y=3.3–3.7, z=0–3: a full-height 0.4 m square column. Retain this envelope and these openings; D1 stays open. New nonstructural partitions and an adjustable interior shade at W1 are available to the design.

Arrange two individual resting places, S1 and S2, and one two-person conversation place, P1: four seats altogether. Give each individual place a visual buffer from D1 and P1 while keeping it connected to the room. Provide three reachable belongings spots, one beside each place; P1's spot holds two bags. Connect all places to D1 with a continuous clear route at least 1.2 m wide and a connected turning circle at least 1.5 m in diameter. The corridor remains active, and W1 supplies the room's daylight. Address these conditions with visible acoustic treatment near the south boundary, adjustable shading, diffuse electric light and a visitor brightness control. Choose the furniture, palette and cleanable contact surfaces. Print "INTERVAL CINEMA" on the four drawing and specification sheets; place "Quiet pause" and "Cinema corridor" at D1. The two visitor views use camera A at (0.8,2.2,1.6) toward (4.8,4.5,1.3) and camera B at (7.3,5.2,1.6) toward (2.4,1.4,1.2), in metres. A shows one visitor at S1; B shows all four seats occupied.

Audience: visitors needing a quieter interval and their companions are the users; the cinema operator and fit-out team will use the work to choose the room arrangement and brief installation.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the room purpose, capacity and fixed requirements. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables with their proportions, formats and stages. existing-room.en.md records the fixed geometry and source-view coordinates. users-and-operations.en.md records seating, belongings, circulation and sensory conditions. existing-plan.png is the constraint image establishing room dimensions and landmark positions. existing-view-a.png is an identity image of the empty room toward W1 and C1. existing-view-b.png is an identity image of the same room toward D1 and C1. solitary-waiting.png is a reference image for a visitor's individual pause. companion-conversation.png is a reference image for quiet conversation between a visitor and companion.

Deliverables:
1. One furnished plan with S1, S2, P1, four seats, three belongings spots, visual buffers, dimensioned route bottlenecks, the turning circle and both camera arrows
2. One south-facing sectional elevation through the entrance-side treatment, with D1, floor and ceiling levels, seat and armrest heights, acoustic construction, brightness control and both entrance signs
3. One reflected ceiling and lighting plan with fixture types, locations and directions, separately controlled ambient, local reading and entrance-cue layers, the visitor control location and W1 daylight and shade annotations
4. One material and furniture sheet with four seat specifications, belongings capacities, named finishes and cleaning methods for contact surfaces, acoustic and shade details, and a shared material and luminaire key
5. One furnished visitor perspective from camera A, with S1 occupied, the W1 wall and C1 visible, and the individual seating buffer and belongings provision legible
6. One furnished visitor perspective from camera B, with S1, S2 and P1 occupied, D1 and C1 visible, and the return route, visitor brightness control and both entrance signs legible

Acceptance:
- The furnished plan, sectional elevation, lighting plan and both perspectives retain the 8.0 m by 6.0 m envelope, 3.0 m ceiling and the recorded positions and dimensions of D1, W1 and C1; D1 remains an open entrance.
- The furnished plan labels S1, S2 and P1, counts four seats and three belongings spots with two-bag capacity at P1, dimensions the narrowest clear route segments at 1.2 m or more and connects a clear turning circle of at least 1.5 m diameter; furniture, buffers and stored bags sit outside those clear areas.
- The furnished plan and both perspectives show a visual buffer between each individual place and D1 and P1, with open access to S1 and S2; perspective A shows one seated visitor and perspective B shows four, using the same furniture and partition positions.
- The sectional elevation, lighting plan, material and furniture sheet and both perspectives agree on south-boundary acoustic treatment, W1 shading and the visitor control location; the lighting plan identifies all three lighting layers, their controls and shielded or indirect light directions.
- The material and furniture sheet assigns material and luminaire IDs, names each finish and its application, and gives cleaning methods for contact surfaces; the plan, sectional elevation and lighting plan repeat the relevant IDs, and perspective A carries a readable acoustic-material callout using the same ID.
- The plan, sectional elevation, lighting plan and material and furniture sheet print INTERVAL CINEMA; the sectional elevation and perspective B display Quiet pause and Cinema corridor at D1, with the return cue pointing through the open entrance.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
